_comment: Stryker mutation testing — flips operators / removes branches in src and reruns the suite to see which mutants the tests CATCH. A surviving mutant = a test that covers the line but asserts nothing that would notice the change (the 'shitty test' signal coverage can't detect). RUNNABLE (PD-114): the code, vitest.config.ts, the root aggregating tsconfig.json, and every mutate target below all exist. Run on demand via `pnpm test:mutation`; calibrate the gate config's break threshold from a measured run. See docs/architecture/core/Spine-Testing.md > Mutation testing + core/Core-Laws-and-Precedents.md.
_plugins_comment: Explicit plugin paths — pnpm's strict node_modules layout breaks Stryker's auto-discovery ('Cannot find Checker plugin typescript' even though it's installed). The third entry is OURS: a relative path, which Stryker's PluginLoader resolves via pathToFileURL + import() (node 26 strips the types, no build step).
_ignorers_comment: The ARID ignorer (tooling/src/mutation-arid/, self-test tests/tooling/mutation-arid/) drops TWO unkillable-by-design families: (1) string-literal mutants whose only destination is an observability sink, and (2) every mutant inside a compile-time-unreachable `never`-typed arm (the exhaustive-dispatch default: case tsc has already proved cannot execute) — trace recorders, trace-collection appends, trace assignments, trace-carrying payload objects, logger calls. Those survive by DESIGN (a test that pinned a debug label byte-for-byte would be the tautology Spine-Testing.md bans), so they are fixed noise in the denominator. It is STRUCTURAL, never an in-source annotation: there is no per-site opt-out an author can reach for.
_checkers_comment: The NATIVE TypeScript 7 checker, on a PATCHED typescript-checker (patches/@stryker-mutator__typescript-checker@10.0.0.patch) and with `@typescript/native` aliased to typescript@7 in the root devDependencies (the checker's loader imports `@typescript/native/unstable/sync` FIRST; its own error message recommends a `typescript7` alias that its code never reads — ignore that message). WHAT THE PATCH FIXES, because the stock preview is silently WRONG here and a bare version bump would re-break it: `ts-native/native-typescript-compiler.js` registers the SANITIZED tsconfig under the RAW `options.tsconfigFile` string (`#adjustTSConfigFile(fileName = this.options.tsconfigFile)`) while the compiler opens `this.tsconfigFile` = `toPosixFileName(path.resolve(...))`. With a relative `tsconfigFile` the two names differ, `NativeFileSystem.readFile` misses, and — per its own comment — the compiler FALLS BACK TO DISK, reading the UNSANITIZED tsconfig. Sanitizing is not optional: `tsconfig-helpers.js` COMPILER_OPTIONS_OVERRIDES forces allowUnreachableCode/noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters (stryker-js#391) precisely because mutants violate them by construction — our tsconfig.base.json sets all three the strict way. Unpatched, `if (cond)` -> `if (false)` mutants are disqualified as CompileError (TS7027) and silently LEAVE THE DENOMINATOR. MEASURED 2026-08-21, kit/macro/engine.ts, 47 mutants, --concurrency 6, quiet box, back-to-back: stock native + relative tsconfig = 11 killed / 0 timeout / 6 survived / 28 compile-error, 57.89, 9m41s. native + ABSOLUTE tsconfig (the falsification arm) = 17 / 1 / 7 / 20, 66.67, 3m03s. native + root-relaxed tsconfig = 18 / 0 / 7 / 20, 66.67, 3m02s. classic = 18 / 0 / 7 / 20, 66.67, 3m17s. So the population difference AND the '2.8x slowdown' were ONE bug — the repeated disk fallback — and the fixed native checker is classic's verdict at classic-or-better speed. Revert to `checkers` without `typescriptChecker` if the patch ever fails to apply.
_mutate_comment: Default scope = the high-stakes pure modules (all exist; PD-114 dropped the phantom domain/chat/routing.ts — prompt assembly is assembly/assemble.ts). Broaden on the CLI, e.g. `pnpm test:mutation --mutate 'packages/server/src/domain/chat/**/*.ts'`. SENTINELS (added 2026-08-21, exploratory ONLY — the gate's mutate list is a CALIBRATED set and stays frozen): the last four entries are the two defect classes no other tier sees. (a) RUNTIME-STRING-KEY arithmetic — stats-delta.ts and rebuild-from-canon.ts accumulate per-turn economics through keys resolved at runtime, where an operator flip produces a plausible number no type or schema notices. (b) SHIPPED-INVERSION — canon-write.ts and memory/recall/recall.ts are exactly where a survived conditional already cost a live bug (the recall.ts inversion), which is the founding case for this whole apparatus. Promote a sentinel into the gate list only WITH a fresh calibration; the gate's `break` is bound to its measured set.
_ignore_comment: ignorePatterns prune the sandbox copy — Stryker COPIES the project tree into .stryker-tmp, so without this it tries to copy node_modules (huge), .stryker-tmp (recursive!), AND the in-repo model/venv caches: .cache/ holds the 8.8G vLLM venv (whose lib64 symlink crashes copyfile with EISDIR) and .models/ holds 25G of HF weights. Keep packages/ + tests/ + the configs. (Now that the sandbox patch makes a NORMAL sandbox work, ignorePatterns is ACTIVE — it was a no-op under the old --inPlace; hence data/** + *.db* are pruned here too.) Stryker does NOT read .gitignore, so the scripts/probes/st-goldens/** block is explicit: it is the ST-parity probe's captured FOREIGN SillyTavern install + its generated fixtures/outputs (.gitignore:104-108; tsconfig.json:135-141 excludes it the same way) — 2,196 files of someone else's runtime, whose unterminated-tag HTML made the DisableTypeChecksPreprocessor warn on every run (audit RC-02; measured on the gate config: 7358 -> 5162 startup files, warning gone).
_coverage_comment: coverageAnalysis is deliberately NOT set — the @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner IGNORES it and always uses perTest (verified in its docs + the installed runner). Each mutant runs only its covering tests; the libSQL native binding survives the runner's forced pool:'threads'.
_dryruntimeout_comment: Same reason as the gate config: Stryker's default dryRunTimeoutMinutes of 5 is far under this project's serial dry run. The runner pins one worker (`pool:'threads'` + `maxWorkers:1`), so the dry run executes one file at a time before any mutant is tested. Since v10 the runner also narrows the dry run to vitest `--related` of the mutate targets (`vitest.related`, DEFAULT TRUE). Do NOT read that as 'the dry run got cheap' — measured on the gate's four targets it still ran 12,060 tests in 17m26s, because they sit deep in the composition graph. What it DOES introduce is a silent failure mode: a target related-mode cannot reach reports NoCoverage rather than failing loudly. See the gate config's `_dryruntimeout_comment` for the receipts.
_concurrency_comment: Box = 24 logical cores / 125GB. Stryker's own default is n-1 (=23); the old pinned 4 used a sixth of the box. 16 → ~8 checker + ~8 runner processes, leaving headroom for the OS + GPU engines / dev work. Bump toward 20 for a dedicated run.
_dashboard_comment: Dashboard reporter (mutation-score badge) is opt-in: add 'dashboard' to reporters + STRYKER_DASHBOARD_API_KEY when there's a public repo.
